name: Cinnamon oil lip plumper

card.summary: Cinnamon-oil plumpers irritate the lips so they swell slightly, creating a temporarily fuller look.
card.note: Irritants can cause burning, redness and allergic reactions.

quick.overview:
Cinnamon oil plumpers are lip glosses that contain cinnamon-derived oil, which tingles and irritates the lips. The irritation brings blood flow and mild swelling, so lips appear fuller for a short time.

They are a non-surgical, temporary alternative to fillers. Wikipedia describes plumpers generally as using irritants such as capsaicin; it does not specifically cover cinnamon.
quick.how: Users apply the gloss like regular lip gloss and wait for the tingling and swelling to appear; effects are temporary and fade within hours.
quick.risks: Irritation, burning, redness and allergic contact reactions are possible with irritant products. People with sensitive skin or allergies to cinnamon-related fragrances may react.

lead: Lip plumpers are cosmetic products that make lips look fuller by irritating the skin; Wikipedia gives capsaicin as an example ingredient and also describes suction pumps as a different approach.[1] Cinnamon oil is another commonly used irritant in glosses, although it is not listed in that article.
The appearance goal is a short-lived fuller lip without injections. Procedures such as fillers or fat grafting last longer, with risks of lumps, ridges or unevenness.[1]
No clinical trials of cinnamon-oil plumpers were found.

angle.text: The swelling is a direct, temporary change in lip volume.

paras: Plumpers rely on mild irritation to cause temporary swelling.[1]
Redness, swelling and itching are common after lip injections; irritant gloss reactions are similar in kind but are not covered in sources found here.[1]
